scope: Frozen low-level endpoint transport challenger; parent owns full protocol/session review and complete test suite

findings.classification: Per-event byte-bound accounting defect; total response bound remains effective
findings.mechanism: line(value) always counts one delimiter byte, but consume recognizes and consumes two-byte CRLF without passing its width. A CRLF-heavy single event is smaller in the counter than on the wire.

observed.fixture: mocked DNS and HTTPS; no socket opened

findings.impact: A server-controlled event can exceed16384 raw bytes and still be accepted. The demonstrated event is21181 bytes; total body remains below65536. No DNS/TLS/pinning bypass or unbounded response was demonstrated.
findings.recommendation: Count actual consumed delimiter bytes, including CRLF split across chunks; add raw exact-boundary and plus-one cases. If the intended limit is explicitly normalized data rather than wire bytes, document that distinction and retain the separate raw body cap.

checkedWithoutAdditionalFindings: All returned A/AAAA addresses are bounded and validated by correct family and public-address policy before selecting a pin. Mixed prohibited/public records fail closed; lookup returns only the selected immutable address and uses no re-resolution.
Literal targets are admitted before bypassing DNS. The socket remote address is checked against the selected family/address, including canonicalized IPv6; TLS authorized must be true.

A new private HTTPS Agent uses proxyEnv empty, TLS verification true, minimumTLS1.2, normal hostname verification, no keepalive/session cache and one total socket. Request options retain original hostname/port/path and fixed family, autoSelectFamily false, and pinned lookup.

Saved Node24.22.2 source confirms private proxy configuration derives from its explicit options and agent options override per-request options. Explicit certificate settings therefore survive the tested request-level weakening.
The request never imports credentials, chooses redirect targets, accepts caller headers/options, installs a permissive certificate callback, or uses globalAgent/fetch.

DNS has a two-second abortable phase; main work is eight seconds; only an established owned legacy session may use an additional two-second cleanup phase. Abort closes request/response; finalization destroys the private agent.

HTTP core maxHeaderSize8192 and strict parsing, own duplicate sensitive-header checks, Content-Encoding rejection and raw body65536 cap bound accepted responses. Non-success/redirect/authentication bodies are not consumed or reflected.
limitations: No complete endpoint suite rerun: parent handles it to avoid redundant tests.
Only the confirmed byte-limit discrepancy was dynamically exercised, using mocked DNS/HTTPS in an owned reviewer script with no socket.
No full security proof, external endpoint readiness, Windows runtime test or immutable published-commit approval is claimed.
System trust additions, local runtime injection and arbitrary local routing/translation remain outside the remote input boundary.
